clue.text: Tide's rough outside the river-put into the bank ?

indicators.note: outside says the shuffled letters go round the outside of the river's name
rough water is churned up, so the letters of the word before it are churned into a new order

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A rough tide outside the river mouth washes something up onto the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' reorders the letters of 'Tide's' and 'outside' wraps them round the river. 'bank' is where money goes, not the riverbank the surface paints.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit money is to lodge it with a bank for safekeeping.

clue.text: Cotton fabric — stupid to have it on your head

parts.note: dim means stupid or slow

indicators.note: your head is the first letter of the word your

explanation.surface: Wearing a cotton cloth on your head would be foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes Y from 'your', placed on top as the last piece in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimity is a sheer, strong cotton cloth woven with raised stripes.

clue.text: Animal breaks section of wall

indicators.note: breaks says the animal breaks into the section, splitting it

parts.note: a part is a section
an ape is an animal

explanation.surface: A beast smashes through part of a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' signals a container: the animal splits the section after its third letter. 'wall' is the definition, not part of the scene of damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along a roof, bridge or balcony edge.

clue.text: Asses blunder about point of pictures

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the point
to blunder is to stumble about clumsily, so the letters of asses are mixed up

parts.note: a cape is a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Fools make a mistake over the meaning of some paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunder' reorders 'Asses' and 'about' wraps the result round the headland, leaving the last S outside. 'point' is a geographical point, not the meaning of the pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Seascapes are paintings of the sea.

clue.text: To change form of RAF is urgent

indicators.note: form of says the following letters are re-formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: Turning the Royal Air Force into something else is pressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges RAF IS URGENT. The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfigure is to transform, altering the outward appearance.

clue.text: Don Juan decamping with illicit gains ?

parts.note: Don Juan, the legendary seducer, is the type of a rake or womaniser
someone decamping is off, gone away

explanation.surface: A notorious seducer makes off with his ill-gotten loot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is a dishonest share or cut skimmed from a deal.

clue.text: Some very early crop'?

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Part of the harvest came in well ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal grass grown as a grain crop.

clue.text: Ring for little Dickensian, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: A bell tolls for a little Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Nell's death in The Old Curiosity Shop famously moved readers, so the tolling bell fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the solemn ring of a bell, especially for a death.

clue.text: Figure for month and past quarter

parts.note: Oct is the short form of October
ago means in the past
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A number totted up for a month and the last three months.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is an eight-sided shape, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Player writes note about new suit

indicators.note: about says the note goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: a flat is a note, as in B flat

indicators.note: new says the letters of suit are made into something new

explanation.surface: A musician jots down a reminder about a new set of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns SUIT into UTIS, and FLAT goes 'about' it. 'writes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A flautist is a musician who plays the flute.

clue.text: Odd dream about poor Alma being in a jam

indicators.note: about says the first shuffled word goes round the second
odd means peculiar or out of order, so the letters of dream are set in an unusual order
poor here means in bad shape, so the name Alma is knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Alma has a strange dream about being in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' and 'poor' each signal an anagram, and 'about' puts the second inside the first. 'jam' looks like a fix to be in, but it is a fruit preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve, a kind of jam made from oranges.

clue.text: Run out of former tar substitute

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-husband

indicators.note: run out of is read as letters running out of order, so tar is rearranged

explanation.surface: A former sailor is chased off and replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' rearranges TAR as TRA. 'tar' looks like the sailor, and 'Run out' like cricket, but the word is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra in a film is a stand-in or spare player, someone held in reserve to fill a gap.

clue.text: Subject with revolver is given in charge

parts.note: a spinning top is something that revolves

explanation.surface: Someone with a gun is put under arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' looks like a gun; it is a toy that spins. 'given in charge' sounds like handing someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Snub includes Jack-that's not very illuminating !

indicators.note: includes says the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to snub someone is to slight them
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a sailor, and so is a tar

explanation.surface: A rebuff that leaves someone in the dark, as unhelpful replies go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' signals a container. The definition is a witty description: light from stars is too faint to see by.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from distant stars is faint, giving very little illumination on a dark night.

clue.text: Making things worse-causes annoyance

definitions.meaning: the act of worsening a problem or an offence
read as a noun phrase, the causes of irritation, the bother itself

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the worsening of something and the irritation or bother that exasperates people.

clue.text: Two ways one's found round a forest, or one over a river

indicators.note: found round says the two ways are placed round the forest, one on each side

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
the second way, another ST
Epping Forest is an ancient woodland on the north-east edge of London
one's gives the letters of the word ones

explanation.surface: Two paths go round a wood, or else someone has to cross a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found round' puts a street abbreviation on each side of the forest. Epping Forest is ancient woodland in Essex on London's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of flat stones laid in a stream is a way to cross it, so the stones as a set are one such crossing.

clue.text: Second star's job ?

definitions.meaning: a moment, an instant: in the blink of an eye
what a star does in the night sky is shine with a flicker

explanation.definitionFit: A twinkling is an instant of time, and the flickering gleam is what stars do.

clue.text: Shows inclination to write song

parts.note: to pen is to write
a chant is a song

explanation.surface: Someone reveals a fondness for songwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows' and 'to' are link words: the wordplay shows the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or fondness for something.

clue.text: Former claims lead to remonstrances

parts.note: ex- means former
postulations are claims or assumptions put forward

explanation.surface: Things someone once demanded end in angry protests.
explanation.definitionFit: Expostulations are protests or reasoned objections made to someone.

clue.text: Aim is simple-to hold up concession

indicators.note: to hold says the first word contains the second

parts.note: pure means simple, as in pure and simple

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to pacify someone

explanation.surface: The goal is basic: to hold out against a compromise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SOP into POS, which PURE holds 'to hold': PUR-POS-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Purpose is the intention or goal one sets out to achieve.

clue.text: Preserve raised estimate for chemical

indicators.note: raised in a down clue says the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to tin food is to preserve it
to rate is to estimate or value

explanation.surface: Keep a higher estimate of a compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TIN into NIT. 'Preserve' is a verb here, not jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a salt of nitric acid, used in fertilisers and explosives.

clue.text: Like rest in form, makes bloomers

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: in form says the letters of rest are formed anew

explanation.surface: Like someone resting in good shape, making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' turns REST into TERS. 'bloomers' looks like blunders or underwear; here it is flowers, things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Asters are daisy-like flowering plants, so they produce blooms.

clue.text: Great disorder in vessel going to a Spanish city

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside the vessel

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel

indicators.note: disorder says the letters of great are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A ship sails in great confusion towards Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' reorders 'Great' and 'in' puts the result inside the tin, then A follows. 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a can.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartagena is a port city in south-east Spain on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: How vigilant on a vigil ?

parts.note: a wake is a watch kept over the dead, a vigil

explanation.surface: How watchful should one be when keeping watch at night?
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' and 'on' are link words: a wake, a night's watch beside the dead, explains the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being awake means not asleep, alert and watchful.

clue.text: Long-tailed birds ?

parts.note: read as the toys flown on strings with long tails, or the raptors with long forked tails

explanation.definitionFit: Kites are both forked-tailed birds of prey and paper toys trailing long tails in the wind.

clue.text: Peculiar charm of a capital to its inhabitants

parts.note: Romans call their capital Roma, the Italian name for Rome

explanation.surface: A city has a special allure for those who live there.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive scent or atmosphere about something, its special quality.

clue.text: Get rid of the main twisters among the best people

indicators.note: among says the twisted letters go inside the best people

parts.note: the elite are the best people of a group

indicators.note: twisters are things that twist, so main is twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Tornadoes are ripping out the finest folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisters' reorders 'main', and 'among' puts it inside the best people, after their third letter. 'twisters' suggests tornadoes.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to remove it entirely.

clue.text: There's some point writing of a German river

definitions.meaning: printers' measures of type width, like the point sizes used in print
the ... flows through north-west Germany to the North Sea

explanation.definitionFit: Ems are units of type measurement in printing, and the Ems is a river in Germany.

clue.text: Article pleads' for return of-ancient hero

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: for return says the word for pleads is turned back to front

parts.note: to sue is to plead or petition

explanation.surface: A document asks for something to be returned from an old champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for return' turns the word for 'pleads' backwards after the article. 'Article' suggests a document, but it is the grammatical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus was the Greek hero who killed the Minotaur in the labyrinth.

clue.text: Dark lady joins Green's trip to Spithead

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters of Green's stumble into another order

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of Spithead, a naval anchorage off Portsmouth

explanation.surface: A woman goes with Green on a boat outing to Spithead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges the letters of Green's, and the first letter of 'Spithead' (a stretch of sea off Portsmouth) follows. The answer is a dated word, now offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, now considered offensive, once named a Black woman, so 'dark lady' describes one.
